unit: pages of 65,536 bytes; a checkpoint image counts in pages (eager: 8,193; post-copy, prefetch, lazy: 1; elastic: 5)
setup: 512 MiB logical heap, 4 pages touched before handoff, receiver touches t of those 4 pages after handoff

rows.refutedBy: any total other than 1,073,807,360 bytes at any t; any receiver fetch (eager does not reset the receiver's frames)
a fetch count other than 5 pages, or a total other than 393,216 bytes
a fetch count other than 6 pages, or a total other than 458,752 bytes
a fetch count other than 8 pages, or a total other than 589,824 bytes (this is the existing four-page row)
any total that differs from post-copy at the same t (the profile is the same four pages, and the receiver refetches the same pages)
any total other than 589,824 bytes at any t; any receiver fetch (the four frames travel in the checkpoint, so the receiver fetches nothing at t = 1, 2 or 4)
any total other than the post-copy total at the same t; this arm is new, so the prediction is that it moves the same pages as post-copy and differs only in resident memory

identity: post-copy total = (4 + t + 1) pages, elastic total = (4 + 5) pages. Equal only at t = 4.
reference: the t = 4 rows of the touched matrix must equal the existing capacity-local rows for eager, post-copy, prefetch and elastic in payload bytes, page counts and checkpoint bytes. Any difference is a change in the executor, not a finding.
policy: round-robin (victim = counter mod frames) evicts in load order. Not measured on the 512 MiB rows: four working pages never evict in four frames, so round-robin and LRU give the same counts there by construction, and the controls' eviction count is recorded to check that.
